key_insight: Geostrophic vortices in rotating turbulence are sustained by inertial-wave Reynolds stresses and selectively absorb waves by angular momentum sign, producing cyclone-dominated, non-monotonic two-dimensionalization at high rotation.
engineering_relevance: This shows that increasing rotation does not always strengthen large-scale coherence, which matters for predicting mixing, energy transfer, and vortex formation in rotating machinery and geophysical flows.
method: Direct numerical simulations of rotating turbulence
Reynolds-averaged momentum balance to test large-scale geostrophic flow maintenance
Wave-field analysis of inertial-wave reflection, critical layers, and viscous absorption
evidence_signal: The abstract reports DNS evidence that inertial-wave Reynolds stresses match the RANS balance, confirm cyclone-anticyclone asymmetry, and show a non-monotonic dependence of geostrophic energy on rotation rate.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on simulated rotating turbulence and may vary with Reynolds number, forcing, and domain geometry in practical systems.
paper_title: Wave-driven geostrophic vortices in rotating turbulence
